mainTopic: Two widows of different statuses, the halacha like רבי אלעזר on מיאון, a minor יבם, and when חליצה is forced
overview: This amud finishes a משנה about a man who died and left two widows. The יבם had relations with one widow, and then he or his brother had relations with the other. Whether the first widow may stay depends on each woman's status: a קטנה, a חרשת, a פקחת or a גדולה. רבי אלעזר says a קטנה who would be disqualified is taught to do מיאון, and the גמרא rules like him and explains why that ruling was needed in two places. A new משנה then rules that a minor יבם stays with his יבמה. It also teaches when בית דין forces חליצה and when it only asks for it: when she says the marriage was never completed, and when she vowed not to benefit from him. The גמרא concludes that this משנה does not follow רבי מאיר. It then proves from פסוקים and from רבא's reasoning that a minor can do יבום. Finally, the גמרא asks which תנא holds the thirty-day rule. רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר, and רבה begins to show it could even fit רבי יוסי, a point that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The first wife stays, and the same is true for two deaf-mute widows
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes the case of two minor widows: the first one stays married to the יבם. It then adds that the same rule applies to two widows who are both חרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not disqualify the first one. The same is true if both widows are deaf-mutes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes the case of two minor widows. The יבם married one first, and then he or his brother had relations with the second. The first one stays married to him, and the משנה says two חרשות follow the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both widows have exactly the same status, so the יבום with the first one does everything that יבום can do here. The later relations with the second widow are forbidden, but they change nothing for the first. Whatever is true for two קטנות is also true for two חרשות.

keyTerms.meaning: Disqualified, meaning he made her forbidden to stay married to the יבם
The first one, the widow the יבם had relations with first
And likewise, so the same rule applies
Deaf-mute women (singular: חֵרֶשֶׁת)

phrases.english: he did not disqualify the first one,
and likewise two deaf-mute women.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא פָּסַל אֶת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וְכֵן שְׁתֵּי חֵרְשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case of two minor widows, which began before this section, and extends its ruling to two deaf-mute widows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both widows have the same status (two קטנות or two חרשות), relations with the second widow do not disqualify the first.

steps.title: Minor first, then deaf-mute: the minor is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: There is one קטנה widow and one חרשת widow. The יבם had relations with the קטנה first, and then he or his brother had relations with the חרשת. The קטנה becomes disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: A minor and a deaf-mute. The יבם had relations with the minor and then with the deaf-mute, or his brother had relations with the deaf-mute. He disqualified the minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts a new pair of widows with different statuses: one is a קטנה and one is a חרשת. If the קטנה came first, the later relations with the חרשת make the קטנה forbidden to the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This result is surprising, because the קטנה came first. The disqualification is a גזירה of the חכמים. They worried people would confuse this case with the reverse order, where the חרשת came first and the disqualification is real (step 3).

keyTerms.meaning: A minor girl
The brother of the man who died, who may do יבום with his widow
His brother, meaning another brother of the man who died
And then he went back and did it again

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the first widow always stays. Here the קטנה came first and is still disqualified, because the second widow has a different weak status.

phrases.english: A minor and a deaf-mute.
The yavam had relations with the minor,
and then had relations with the deaf-mute,
or his brother had relations with the deaf-mute —
he disqualified the minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְטַנָּה וְחֵרֶשֶׁת. בָּא יָבָם עַל הַקְּטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from two widows of the same status to two widows of different statuses, and reaches the opposite result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minor first, then deaf-mute: the minor is disqualified by a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: Deaf-mute first, then minor: the deaf-mute is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: This is the reverse order of step 2. The יבם had relations with the חרשת first, and then he or his brother had relations with the קטנה. The חרשת becomes disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The יבם had relations with the deaf-mute and then with the minor, or his brother had relations with the minor. He disqualified the deaf-mute.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the order from step 2. Now the חרשת came first, and the later relations with the קטנה make the חרשת forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marriage with a חרשת is only a partial acquisition. Because the קטנה has a different status, this partial acquisition does not free her from יבום. So the relations with her also count as a partial acquisition. Both widows end up forbidden, since יבום may not be done with two widows.

keyTerms.meaning: Had relations with
The deaf-mute woman
Or that, which introduces the second possibility (the brother instead of the יבם)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the real reason a disqualification happens between a קטנה and a חרשת. The rule in step 2 is a decree based on this case.

phrases.english: The yavam had relations with the deaf-mute,
and then had relations with the minor,
or his brother had relations with the minor —
he disqualified the deaf-mute.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא יָבָם עַל הַחֵרֶשֶׁת, וְחָזַר וּבָא עַל הַקְּטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror case of step 2 with the order reversed. The first widow is disqualified again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Deaf-mute first, then minor: the deaf-mute is disqualified, because each act was only a partial acquisition.

steps.title: Competent woman first, then deaf-mute: the competent woman stays
steps.stepSummary: There is one פקחת widow and one חרשת widow. If the יבם had relations with the פקחת first, the later relations with the חרשת do not disqualify the פקחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A competent woman and a deaf-mute. The יבם had relations with the competent woman and then with the deaf-mute, or his brother had relations with the deaf-mute. He did not disqualify the competent woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a new pair: a fully competent widow and a deaf-mute widow. When the פקחת came first, she stays married to the יבם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום with a פקחת is a complete יבום. It fully ends the bond with both widows. So the later relations with the חרשת are forbidden but have no legal effect on the פקחת.

keyTerms.meaning: A fully competent woman, not a minor and not a deaf-mute
Did not disqualify, so she may stay married

steps.whatToRemember: The first widow stays when both widows have the same status, or when the first one is a פקחת whose יבום is complete. When one widow is a קטנה and the other a חרשת, the first one is disqualified in either order.

phrases.english: A competent woman and a deaf-mute.
The yavam had relations with the competent woman,
and then had relations with the deaf-mute,
or his brother had relations with the deaf-mute —
he did not disqualify the competent woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: פִּקַּחַת וְחֵרֶשֶׁת. בָּא יָבָם עַל הַפִּקַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to a pair where the first widow is fully competent, in contrast with the קטנה and חרשת pair, and returns to the result that the first widow stays.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Competent woman first, then deaf-mute: the competent woman is not disqualified, because her יבום was complete.

steps.title: Deaf-mute first, then the competent wife
steps.stepSummary: The יבם had relations with the חרשת first and then with the פקחת, or his brother had relations with the פקחת. The חרשת is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the יבם had relations with the deaf-mute wife and then with the competent wife, or his brother had relations with the competent wife, the deaf-mute wife becomes disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reverse of step 4. This time the חרשת came first and the פקחת came second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with a חרשת only make a partial bond, so the יבום link to the family is not fully cut. The later relations with the פקחת still count fully. Because of that, the חרשת is the one who loses out.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is legally competent (not deaf-mute)
Disqualified her (she cannot stay married to him)
And then he went on to have relations

phrases.english: If the יבם had relations with the deaf-mute
and then had relations with the competent woman,
or his brother had relations with the competent woman,
he disqualified the deaf-mute.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא יָבָם עַל הַחֵרֶשֶׁת וְחָזַר וּבָא עַל הַפִּקַּחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverse order of step 4 (חרשת first instead of פקחת first)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the חרשת came first and the פקחת second, the חרשת is disqualified.

steps.title: Adult and minor: the adult came first
steps.stepSummary: A new pair: a גדולה and a קטנה. If the יבם had relations with the גדולה first, later relations with the קטנה do not disqualify the גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: An adult and a minor. If the יבם had relations with the adult and then with the minor, or his brother had relations with the minor, the adult is not disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens a new pair: one adult widow and one minor widow. It starts with the case where the adult came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גדולה's marriage to the dead brother was a full marriage. So the יבם's relations with her fully finish the יבום. Nothing that happens later with the קטנה can disqualify her.

keyTerms.meaning: An adult woman (her marriage is fully valid by תורה law)
Did not disqualify her

phrases.english: An adult and a minor.
If the יבם had relations with the adult,
and then had relations with the minor,
or his brother had relations with the minor,
he did not disqualify the adult.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּדוֹלָה וּקְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 4, now applied to a גדולה and a קטנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the גדולה came first, she remains permitted to the יבם.

steps.title: Adult and minor: the minor came first
steps.stepSummary: Reverse order: the יבם had relations with the קטנה first and then with the גדולה. The קטנה is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the יבם had relations with the minor and then with the adult, or his brother had relations with the adult, the minor is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reverse of step 6. This time the קטנה came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קטנה's marriage is only a rabbinic marriage, so relations with her do not fully finish the יבום. The later relations with the גדולה still count. So the קטנה ends up disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor girl (her marriage is only rabbinic)

steps.whatToRemember: In the פקחת/חרשת pair and the גדולה/קטנה pair, the wife with the weaker marriage (חרשת or קטנה) is disqualified if she came first. The wife with the full marriage (פקחת or גדולה) is not disqualified if she came first. In the קטנה/חרשת pair, the first widow is disqualified in either order (steps 2-3).

phrases.english: If the יבם had relations with the minor,
and then had relations with the adult,
or his brother had relations with the adult,
he disqualified the minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּא יָבָם עַל הַקְּטַנָּה וְחָזַר וּבָא עַל הַגְּדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverse order of step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the קטנה came first and the גדולה second, the קטנה is disqualified.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: teach the minor to refuse
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the minor is taught to do מיאון, refusing the יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: We teach the minor to refuse him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a different approach to the case in step 7, where the קטנה came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By doing מיאון, the קטנה cancels her original marriage. Then she is no longer tied up in this mess, and the problem is fixed through her refusal.

keyTerms.meaning: We teach / instruct her
That she should do מיאון (refuse and cancel her marriage as a minor)
A minor's refusal, which undoes her rabbinic marriage

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
We instruct the minor to refuse him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מְלַמְּדִין הַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁתְּמָאֵן בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different solution to the case in step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטנה is told to do מיאון.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules like רבי אלעזר of the משנה. רבי אלעזר the אמורא says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: The הלכה is like רבי אלעזר. And רבי אלעזר also said: The הלכה is like רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by deciding the halacha in favor of רבי אלעזר's view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate אמוראים give the same ruling. So in practice, the קטנה is taught to do מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
And likewise said (a second person gives the same ruling)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two people named רבי אלעזר here. One is the תנא in the משנה (רבי אלעזר בן שמוע). The other is the אמורא who rules like him (רבי אלעזר בן פדת).

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.
And likewise Rabbi Elazar said:
phrases.notes: This is the later רבי אלעזר, an אמורא, not the one from the משנה.

phrases.english: The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the practical halacha on the מחלוקת in steps 7-8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר: the קטנה is taught to do מיאון.

steps.title: Why the ruling had to be said in both places
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why שמואל's ruling was needed both in the earlier case and here. If it were said only in the earlier case, we would think it applies there only because יבום was not yet done. Here יבום was done, so we might think both wives must leave with a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary to say it in both places. If it had been said only in the first case, we would think שמואל ruled like רבי אליעזר there because the יבם had not yet done the מצוה of יבום. But here, where the מצוה of יבום was done, we might say both wives must leave with a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכותא, explaining why two similar rulings are both needed. It gives the first half here and sets up the second half, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, the יבם could not do יבום at all unless the minor refused, so teaching her to refuse makes sense there. Here, he already did יבום with the קטנה, so there is less need to help him. We might think the simpler answer is to release both wives with a גט. That is why the ruling had to be stated here too.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (both statements are needed)
In that first (earlier) case
The מצוה of marrying the dead brother's widow
Let them leave with a bill of divorce

steps.confusionAlert: The 'first case' is not step 7. It is an earlier משנה on דף 109a about a man married to a minor whose adult sister falls to him for יבום.

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
phrases.notes: Necessary for שמואל to rule like this both here and in the earlier case on דף 109a.

phrases.english: for if it had been stated only in that first case,
it is in that case that Shmuel says
the halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer,
phrases.notes: In that earlier משנה, the same idea, teaching the minor to refuse, is said in the name of רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: because he did not fulfill the mitzvah of יבום,
but in this case, where the mitzvah of יבום was fulfilled,
I would say both of them must leave with a גט,

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא דְּאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ruling in step 9 is not redundant with שמואל's ruling on the earlier case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ruling given only in the earlier case could not be applied here, because here יבום was already done and we might have released both wives with a גט.

steps.title: The other half of why the ruling was needed in both cases
steps.stepSummary: If the ruling had been taught only here, we would have limited it to this case, where the גדולה is also a יבמה waiting for him. So it was needed in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the ruling had been taught only in this case, we would say it applies because the adult is also available to him. But in the other case it would not apply. So both statements are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its two-sided explanation from the previous step. It shows that each statement of שמואל's ruling teaches something the other one could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 explained why the earlier case alone was not enough. Now we hear the reverse. Here the גדולה is herself a יבמה before him, so pushing the קטנה to do מיאון just clears the way to the גדולה. In the earlier case the קטנה is already his wife, and the גדולה is his wife's sister. There we might have thought the קטנה should not be pushed to refuse. That is why both statements are 'צריכא', needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It taught us
Is available to him, literally 'lies before him'
The other one (the other case)
It is necessary: both statements are needed

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכותא shows that two similar statements each teach something new. Neither one could be learned from the other, so both are needed.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only in this case,
we would say it is because the adult is available to him.
But in the other case, not.
phrases.notes: 'The other case' is the earlier ruling discussed in step 10.

phrases.english: So it is necessary to say both.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכותא begun in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's ruling like רבי אלעזר had to be stated in both cases, because each case had a reason that might have limited it.

steps.title: A minor יבם who lived with his יבמה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. If a minor יבם lived with a minor יבמה, they grow up together. If he lived with an adult יבמה, she raises him.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a minor יבם had relations with a minor יבמה, they grow up together. If he had relations with an adult יבמה, she raises him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It rules that when the יבם is a minor, the couple stays together until they grow up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the יבם is a minor, his act creates a connection that keeps them together. Whether she is a minor or an adult, they remain as a couple until he grows up.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A יבם who is a minor
They grow up together
She raises him

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: יָבָם קָטָן, שֶׁבָּא עַל יְבָמָה קְטַנָּה —
phrases.english: A minor yavam who had relations with a minor yevama:
they grow up with each other.
If he had relations with an adult yevama:
she raises him.
phrases.notes: She stays married to him while he grows up.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ יָבָם קָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor יבם who lived with his יבמה stays with her. If she is a minor, they grow up together. If she is an adult, she raises him.

steps.title: A יבמה who says the marriage was never completed
steps.stepSummary: If she makes the claim within thirty days, he is forced to do חליצה. After thirty days, he is only asked. If he admits she is right, he is forced even after twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a יבמה said within thirty days, 'He never had relations with me,' בית דין forces him to do חליצה for her. If she said it after thirty days, they ask him to do חליצה. And if he admits it, they force him to do חליצה even after twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a יבמה who says the יבום was never completed. It rules on whether בית דין forces the יבם to do חליצה or only asks him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Within thirty days her claim is believable, so בית דין forces him. After thirty days, we assume the marriage was probably completed, so if he disagrees with her, he is only asked. But if he agrees with her, there is no argument, and he is forced no matter how much time has passed.

keyTerms.meaning: He never had relations with me
בית דין forces him
בית דין asks him, without forcing
He admits

steps.confusionAlert: 'Forcing' and 'asking' are two different levels. Forcing means בית דין pressures him until he does חליצה. Asking means it is only a request.

phrases.english: A yevama who said within thirty days
'I have not had relations with him':
they force him to do chalitza for her.
After thirty days:
they ask him to do chalitza for her.
And when he admits it:
even after twelve months
they force him to do chalitza for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְּבָמָה שֶׁאָמְרָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next ruling in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If her claim comes within thirty days, or if he admits it, he is forced to do חליצה. If her claim comes after thirty days and he disagrees, he is only asked.

steps.title: A יבמה who vowed not to benefit from her יבם
steps.stepSummary: If she made the vow while her husband was alive, the יבם is forced to do חליצה. If she made it after her husband died, he is only asked. If she vowed on purpose to avoid יבום, he is only asked even if the vow was made while her husband was alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a woman vowed while her husband was alive not to benefit from her יבם, they force him to do חליצה for her. If she vowed after her husband died, they ask him to do חליצה. And if she meant to avoid יבום, then even if she vowed while her husband was alive, they only ask him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה rules on a woman whose own vow keeps her from marrying the יבם. Whether he is forced to do חליצה depends on when she vowed and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow made while her husband was alive was not aimed at blocking יבום, so it is not her fault, and he is forced. A vow made after the husband's death looks like a deliberate move to block יבום, so he is only asked. If she planned this from the start, even an early vow counts as deliberate.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who vows not to benefit from someone
While her husband was alive
Her husband's death
She meant it for this purpose (to avoid יבום)

steps.whatToRemember: In both of these cases, בית דין forces him when she is not to blame. When the problem looks like her own doing, בית דין only asks him.

phrases.english: A woman who vows not to benefit from her yavam,
during her husband's lifetime:
they force him to do chalitza for her.
After her husband's death:
they ask him to do chalitza for her.
And if she intended this:
phrases.notes: She made the vow on purpose, so that she would not have to do יבום.

phrases.english: even during her husband's lifetime
they ask him to do chalitza for her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנּוֹדֶרֶת הֲנָאָה מִיְּבָמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third ruling in the same משנה, again comparing forcing with asking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow made while her husband was alive means he is forced to do חליצה. A vow made after the husband's death, or one made on purpose to avoid יבום, means he is only asked.

steps.title: Is our משנה against רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests our משנה does not follow רבי מאיר, who says minors may not do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Let us say our משנה is not like רבי מאיר. A ברייתא teaches: a minor boy and a minor girl do not do חליצה and do not do יבום. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out that our משנה seems to go against a ruling of רבי מאיר found in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said a minor יבם who lived with a minor יבמה can grow up with her, so it lets minors do יבום. רבי מאיר says minors do not do יבום at all. So it looks like the משנה cannot follow רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say. It introduces a suggestion the גמרא wants to test.
They do חליצה.
They do יבום.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: GEMARA: Let us say our משנה is not like רבי מאיר.
phrases.notes: Our משנה is the one from step 12, where a minor יבם lived with a minor or adult יבמה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: a minor boy and a minor girl
do not do חליצה and do not do יבום,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the new משנה from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a minor יבם may do יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר in a ברייתא says minors do not do יבום, which seems to clash with the משנה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר only spoke about a minor with an adult
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר forbids only a minor paired with an adult, not two minors together.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי מאיר. When רבי מאיר spoke, he meant an adult woman with a minor boy, or a minor girl with an adult man, because for one of them the act is forbidden. But a minor boy with a minor girl, where both are the same, he did not say it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the משנה by limiting רבי מאיר's ruling to mixed cases, a minor with an adult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one side is an adult, the act is forbidden for that adult, so רבי מאיר forbids it. When both are minors, they are in the same position, so רבי מאיר never forbade it. That fits the משנה's case of two minors growing up together.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. It shows the rule can fit the opinion that seemed to disagree.
A forbidden act of relations.
Like each other, the same.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows רבי מאיר.
When רבי מאיר said this,
he meant an adult woman with a minor boy, or a minor girl with an adult man,
because for one of them it is a forbidden act.
But a minor boy who lives with a minor girl,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ כִּי הֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ, לָא אָמַר.
phrases.english: where both of them are the same, he did not say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבי מאיר's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר forbids any יבום involving a minor.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר only forbids a minor with an adult. Two minors together are allowed.

steps.title: But the משנה lets an adult יבמה raise the minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the משנה itself allows a minor with an adult יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה teaches: if he lived with an adult יבמה, she should raise him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 16 by quoting the משנה's second case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer said רבי מאיר forbids a minor with an adult. But the משנה clearly allows a minor יבם with an adult יבמה, since she raises him. So even with the answer, the משנה still clashes with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is taught. It brings a source to challenge what was just said.
She should raise him.
An adult יבמה.

phrases.english: But it is taught:
If he lived with an adult יבמה, she should raise him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה can follow רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows the very case, a minor with an adult, that the answer said רבי מאיר forbids.

steps.title: After the fact is different
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא חוזאה answers that once the minor has already lived with her, the rule is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא חוזאה said: once he already lived with her, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא חוזאה tries to save the answer by saying the משנה speaks after it already happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר forbids a minor and an adult from doing יבום from the start. But the משנה's words 'if he lived with her' describe something already done. After the fact, she raises him, which does not clash with רבי מאיר's ruling about the start.

keyTerms.meaning: He already lived with her, it already happened.
It is different.

phrases.english: רבי חנינא חוזאה said:
Once he already lived with her, it is different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא חוֹזָאָה: בָּא שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the start of the act from after the act.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה allows a minor and an adult from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר forbids it from the start. The משנה only says what happens once it is done.

steps.title: Raising him means living together again and again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that answer: 'she raises him' means they keep living together, and each time would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says she should raise him, and every single act would be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down רבי חנינא חוזאה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'After the fact' could only cover the first act. But 'she should raise him' means they stay together as a couple. If רבי מאיר forbids a minor with an adult, every later act would also be forbidden, so the משנה could not tell them to stay together.

keyTerms.meaning: Each and every act of relations.
It says.

phrases.english: But it says she should raise him,
and each and every act would be forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְּגַדְּלֶנּוּ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the 'after the fact' answer completely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'She raises him' allows living together going forward, not just one act already done.

steps.title: The משנה is not like רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that our משנה does not follow רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that our משנה is not like רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up trying to fit the משנה with רבי מאיר and accepts the first suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both attempts to fit the משנה with רבי מאיר failed. So the suggestion from step 15 stands: the משנה follows a view that disagrees with רבי מאיר and allows minors to do יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier answer.
It is clear.

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה lets a minor יבם do יבום, even with an adult יבמה. This does not follow רבי מאיר, who says minors do not do יבום.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר.
phrases.english: Rather, it is clear that our משנה is not like רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְחַוַּורְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the rejection in step 19.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Our משנה does not follow רבי מאיר.

steps.title: A minor cannot build a name for his brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a minor can do יבום when the פסוק speaks of building a name for the dead brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Read here the פסוק 'to build a name for his brother,' and this minor cannot do that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the משנה: how can a minor do יבום at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה describes יבום as building a name for the dead brother, which means having children. A minor cannot have children. So it seems his יבום should not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Read here, apply this פסוק to the case.
To build a name for his brother.
Able to do this.

phrases.english: Read here: 'to build a name for his brother',
and this one is not able to do that!

steps.triggerLanguage: קְרִי כָּאן לְהָקִים לְאָחִיו שֵׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a minor יבם can do יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק links יבום to building a name for the brother, which a minor cannot do.

steps.title: Any יבם at all counts
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers from the פסוק 'her יבם shall come upon her' that any יבם at all counts, even a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the פסוק says 'her יבם shall come upon her,' meaning any יבם at all.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question by bringing a different פסוק about יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'her יבם shall come upon her' does not say anything about having children. It just says her יבם comes upon her, so any יבם at all can do the יבום. That is why a minor's ביאה counts even though he cannot yet have children.

keyTerms.meaning: Her יבם shall come upon her.
Any at all, whoever he is.

steps.whatToRemember: A minor יבם's ביאה counts as יבום, because the פסוק 'her יבם shall come upon her' includes any ביאה, even by someone who cannot have children.

phrases.english: אביי said: the פסוק says:
'Her יבם shall come upon her', any at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a different פסוק that is broader.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only someone who can build a name for his brother can do יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any ביאה at all counts as יבום, even a minor's.

steps.title: רבא: Nothing in יבום is forbidden now and permitted later
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a different answer from אביי's. Even without אביי's reading of the פסוק, you cannot say a minor is excluded from יבום, because יבום does not work as 'forbidden now, permitted later.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Even without this, you still could not say it. Is there anything that is forbidden to him now and becomes permitted after a while?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own answer to the question of how a minor can do יבום. He argues from logic instead of from אביי's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose a minor could not do יבום. Then when his brother died, the widow would be forbidden to him. רבא points out that a יבמה cannot be forbidden at first and then become permitted when he grows up. So excluding minors would lead to an impossible result.

keyTerms.meaning: even without this (even without the previous answer)
you cannot say
forbidden
permitted

phrases.english: Rava said:
Even without this,
you could not say it (that a minor cannot do יבום).
phrases.notes: The גמרא just says 'you could not say it'; what it means, from the question being answered, is that a minor cannot do יבום.

phrases.english: Is there any case
where she is forbidden to him now
and after a while she becomes permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: בְּלָאו הָכִי נָמֵי לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the question in step 21, alongside אביי's answer in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical argument from what would follow (reductio)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A minor cannot fulfill 'establishing a name,' so maybe he is excluded from יבום.
steps.terutzMaskana: Excluding him would make the יבמה forbidden now and permitted later, and יבום has no such case. So a minor must be included.

steps.title: רב's rule: a יבמה unfit at the time of falling is forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: רבא backs up his point with רב יהודה's quote from רב. If a יבמה is not fit for יבום at the moment she falls to the brother, she is like the wife of a brother who had children, and she is forbidden to him permanently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did not רב יהודה say in the name of רב: Any יבמה to whom I cannot apply 'her יבם shall come upon her' at the time of falling is like the wife of a brother who has children, and she is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source that proves his claim that a יבמה cannot become permitted later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What decides everything is the moment of נפילה, when the brother dies. If יבום is impossible then, the widow falls back into the plain prohibition of a brother's wife, which lasts forever. So if a minor could not do יבום, his brother's widow would be forbidden to him for life.

keyTerms.meaning: the moment the widow falls to the brother for יבום (when the husband dies)
a brother's wife, normally a forbidden relation
who had children, so there is no יבום at all

steps.whyThisMatters: רב's rule is a basic principle in יבום: the widow's status is set once, at the moment of נפילה.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
Any יבמה to whom I cannot apply
at the time she falls to him
'Her יבם shall come upon her' —
is like the wife of a brother
who had children, and she is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind רבא's claim in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that a יבמה cannot be forbidden now and permitted later.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה in the name of רב: a יבמה unfit for יבום at the moment of נפילה is permanently forbidden, like the wife of a brother who had children.

steps.title: Maybe a minor's יבמה really is forbidden forever
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. Maybe that is exactly the halacha: a minor cannot do יבום, and so his brother's widow is forbidden to him forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say that this is indeed so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא by accepting his 'impossible' result and asking why it can't simply be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's argument only works if it is obvious that a minor's brother's widow is not forbidden forever. The גמרא asks: what is wrong with saying she is? This forces a source showing that a minor brother is part of יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: and say that it is indeed so

phrases.english: And say that it is indeed so!
phrases.notes: Meaning: maybe the minor really is left out of יבום, and the widow really is forbidden to him forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption under רבא's argument in steps 23-24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's assumption that a minor's brother's widow cannot be permanently forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing so far rules out that result, so it could be the real halacha.

steps.title: Even a one-day-old brother is included in יבום
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'כי ישבו אחים יחדו' includes every brother alive at the same time as the deceased, even a baby one day old. So a minor brother is part of יבום, and his brother's widow is not forbidden to him forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'If brothers dwell together' — even one day old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק showing that even a newborn brother is part of יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Dwell together' only requires that the brothers were alive at the same time, not that they were adults. Since even a one-day-old brother is included, a minor cannot be excluded. This keeps רבא's argument standing.

keyTerms.meaning: brothers dwell together
one day old

steps.whatToRemember: A minor brother, even a one-day-old baby, is part of יבום. רבא proves a minor can do יבום because otherwise the widow would be forbidden forever, and the פסוק 'כי ישבו אחים יחדו' rules that out.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'If brothers dwell together' —
even one day old.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: כִּי יֵשְׁבוּ אַחִים יַחְדָּו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A minor might be excluded from יבום, leaving the widow forbidden forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Dwell together' includes even a one-day-old brother, so a minor is part of יבום.

steps.title: Which תנא holds a man can hold back for thirty days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a יבמה who says within thirty days that he has not been with her. It asks which תנא holds that a man may hold himself back for up to thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A יבמה who said within thirty days, etc.' Who is the תנא who holds that for up to thirty days a person can restrain himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's thirty-day rule. It asks whose opinion that rule follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה trusts the יבמה's claim within thirty days. This assumes it is believable that a man would not be with his wife for that long. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: etc. (the rest of the משנה's words)
who is the תנא (whose opinion is this)
a person controls himself

phrases.aramaic: יְבָמָה שֶׁאָמְרָה בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'A יבמה who said within thirty days,' etc.
phrases.notes: She is saying, 'he has not been with me,' and the משנה rules that he is forced to do חליצה.

phrases.english: Who is the תנא
who holds that for up to thirty days
a person can restrain himself?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תַּנָּא דְּעַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין מוֹקֵים אִינִישׁ אַנַּפְשֵׁיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the thirty-day assumption behind the משנה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: It is רבי מאיר, as with a virginity claim
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה follows רבי מאיר. A ברייתא quotes רבי מאיר saying that a טענת בתולים can be made for all of the first thirty days, which shows he sees thirty days as the normal window.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It is רבי מאיר. As it is taught: A claim about virginity may be made all thirty days; these are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן names the תנא behind the thirty-day rule: רבי מאיר. He proves it from a ברייתא about a טענת בתולים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets a husband raise a virginity claim during the first thirty days of marriage. This matches the משנה's thirty-day rule for the יבמה. So the משנה is placed with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: a husband's claim that his bride was not a virgin

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: It is Rabbi Meir.
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A claim about virginity
may be made all thirty days;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי מאיר, who gives thirty days for a טענת בתולים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: If They Were Alone, the Claim Must Be Made Right Away
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with רבי יוסי. If the bride was alone with her husband, a טענת בתולים is only believed if made immediately. If they were never alone, it can be made even years later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: if she was secluded with him, the claim must be made immediately. If she was not secluded with him, the claim can be made even after several years.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that quoted רבי מאיר now gives the other side, רבי יוסי. This sets up why the גמרא said the משנה follows רבי מאיר and not רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר gives a thirty-day window for a טענת בתולים. רבי יוסי gives no window at all once the couple has been alone. They are presumed to have been together, so any claim must come at once. That makes it look like רבי יוסי could not agree with a משנה that lets a man hold back for thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: She was secluded, alone with him in a private place
Immediately, right away
Even after several years

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If she was secluded — immediately;
phrases.notes: He means that if she was alone with her husband, a claim that she was not a virgin is only believed if he makes it right away.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִסְתְּרָה — אַף לְאַחַר כַּמָּה שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: if she was not secluded — even after several years.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 28 by giving the opposing view of רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, if the couple was alone together, a טענת בתולים must be made immediately. If they were never alone, it can be made even years later.

steps.title: רבה: The משנה Can Even Follow רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבה disagrees with רבי יוחנן and says the משנה could follow רבי יוסי too. רבי יוסי only spoke about a man and his own ארוסה, whom he is used to. A brother's wife may be different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי only said his rule there about a man's betrothed, whom he is used to. But his brother's wife —
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a second answer to the question of which תנא the משנה follows. He starts to explain why רבי יוסי's rule might not apply to a יבם and his brother's widow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's 'immediately' rule makes sense when a man is with his own ארוסה, because he is familiar and comfortable with her. רבה is about to argue that a man and his brother's wife are not like that. So even רבי יוסי could allow a waiting period there. The text stops in the middle of this point.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say: the ruling fits even the opinion you thought it contradicts
He only said his rule up to this point and no further; it limits an opinion to its own case
His betrothed, his own bride
Whom he is used to and comfortable with
His brother's wife, here the widow who comes to him for יבום

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying רבי יוחנן's answer is impossible. He is offering another way to read the משנה, in which it fits even רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Yosei.

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei only says his rule there
about his betrothed, whom he is used to.
but his brother's wife —
phrases.notes: רבה's sentence isn't finished here; it continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer from רבי יוחנן (step 28) to the question in step 27. It does this by limiting רבי יוסי's rule (step 29) to a man's own ארוסה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a man may hold himself back from his יבמה for up to thirty days?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even רבי יוסי could agree. His 'immediately' rule applies only to a man's own ארוסה, whom he is comfortable with, and not to a brother's wife.
